parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police targeting or border or facility rules, and no documented visitor-facing violence campaign. Mitigating: the 2015 decriminalisation, a 2017 high-court ruling protecting the LGBT organisation, the incitement article (Art. 191) covering gender identity, and an activist's 2015 statement that the community is not targeted by violence. Exposures: no statutory anti-discrimination protection for gender identity in education, health, housing or employment; the 2023/2024 repeal of employment protection; no legal gender recognition; and family ostracisation. These are mostly resident-facing, so they weigh lightly. Open questions (custody placement, entry document treatment, emergency care, enforcement of Arts. 191/160) are unanswered rather than established exposures. The only violence assessment is dated 2015, and no trans-specific violence figure exists. The thin trans-specific record is extrapolated from the lack of criminalisation and of documented targeting, pulled down by unremedied service-discrimination exposure. Net: mid-to-upper elevated-to-reduced band.
